doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Howard Theatre, Baltimore and Edgewood
summary: Fuller played the Howard with Olatunji, Jimmy Smith and Dizzy's band, and played around Baltimore while stationed at Edgewood.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you have any experiences at the Howard Theatre performing?

Yeah, plenty. I played with a lot of different people at the Howard Theatre. I played here once with Olatunji and I played here once with Jimmy Smith. Outside of Art Blakey if that’s what you mean. On several different things, I came here with Dizzy’s band. I don’t know if we came here with Quincy but I know that we went to Baltimore at that club there, at the Regal Theatre there.
Yeah, the Royal. I said Regal…Yeah. We did that. So, I was around here and they knew and they would always pit me with Calvin Jones. There was another guy from Baltimore, Repart Stone.

Yeah so we were all—See, I was stationed to the Army Chemical Center last in Edgewood Maryland and I would come in there and do my little thing and go back out to Edgewood and I would play with guys around there. Pete Peterson and Wendell, Bill Swindell and a little piano player that was married to the little piano player. What’s his name?

no. No, but I knew quite a few musicians run here. But, between here and Baltimore, I knew a lot of players. Sully Blaire was around here then. She was from Baltimore. Gary Bartz father have club. I played there a lot there in Baltimore.
A lot of the culture used to come in there and stuff, you know? I was around there for a while, two or three years, you know? So I knew the musicians, you know?
